name: Gather Grove Booking
author: gturtle108

sections.description:
Gather Grove Booking runs the schedule for people who teach — yoga and fitness studios, dance and martial arts schools, music teachers, pottery and craft studios, wellness practitioners, and community programs. Design your booking pages visually with Elementor, take drop-in and appointment bookings, and accept card payments with Stripe.

The free version is fully functional for running a real studio:

  • Classes & sessions — recurring schedules, capacity limits, multiple locations and rooms.
  • Online booking — Elementor booking-form and schedule widgets your clients use to reserve a spot.
  • Appointments — bookable service slots with availability windows and optional deposits.
  • Waivers & liability forms — collect a real signature as part of booking, then see your whole roster at a glance: who has signed the current version, who signed an older one, whose signature has expired, and who has never signed at all. Send reminders by hand, record a paper signature, or export the lot to CSV.
  • Passwordless sign-in — students can sign in with a link emailed to them instead of a password, so nobody is locked out of a booking by a password they never set. Optional, and you choose whether your site offers passwords, magic links, or both.
  • Waitlists — clients can join a waitlist when a class is full, and open spots are automatically offered to the next person in line.
  • Flexible schedules — a class can meet on multiple recurring schedule blocks (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri at different times).
  • Bulk attendance marking — mark a whole roster present in one action.
  • Payments — accept cards through Stripe for drop-in bookings.
  • Client accounts — a self-service dashboard for bookings and profile.
  • Attendance — front-desk and instructor check-in.
  • Instructors & locations — profiles, assignments, and per-location schedules.

Who it’s for

  • Yoga, pilates and fitness studios — recurring drop-in classes, capacity limits, waitlists, and a signed waiver on file before anyone steps on a mat.
  • Dance and martial arts schools — several weekly schedule blocks on one class, per-location rooms, and front-desk check-in.
  • Music teachers and schools — appointment-style lessons with availability windows and optional deposits, alongside recurring group classes.
  • Pottery, craft and maker studios — small capacities, multiple rooms, and a roster you can mark present in one action.
  • Wellness practitioners — one-to-one appointments shown in the visitor’s own timezone, with a self-service client dashboard.
  • Breathwork, meditation and sound-healing facilitators — circles, workshops and sound baths with capacity limits, a waitlist when they fill, and a waiver signed before anyone arrives.
  • Coaches, mentors and private sessions — bookable one-to-one slots with availability windows and optional deposits, so clients pick a time without the back-and-forth.
  • Online facilitators — virtual classes and appointments, with the Zoom meeting created for you and the join link in every confirmation and reminder.
  • Community programs and co-ops — free and comp bookings with no payment gateway required, and waiver compliance across a whole roster.

Built for Elementor

The client-facing pages (booking form, class schedule, appointment booking, client dashboard) are Elementor widgets, so you design them visually alongside the rest of your site. The free Elementor plugin (3.5 or newer) is required to display these on your site. Elementor Pro is optional — it adds dynamic tags and one-click Theme Builder starter pages, but is not required for booking to work.

Part of the Gather Grove suite

Gather Grove Booking works entirely on its own. It is also one part of Gather Grove, a family of plugins for running and growing a creative business on your own WordPress site. The plugins share one admin, one list of people, and one look, so a studio can add what it needs as it grows:

  • Gather Grove Pulse — email broadcasts, automated sequences and a contact list that knows who booked, joined or enrolled.
  • Gather Grove Communities — private member spaces with rooms, an activity feed and direct messages.
  • Gather Grove Courses — self-paced and cohort-based online courses.
  • Gather Grove Forms — applications, intake forms and RSVPs that feed the rest of the suite.
  • Gather Grove Companion — an AI assistant for your admin, and a chat helper for your visitors.
  • Gather Grove Notion Sync — free; sends bookings and form entries to your Notion workspace.

Together they serve creators, mentors, facilitators and anyone running a private community or an online program, as well as studios. Learn more at gathergrove.io.

Free and Professional

Everything listed above is free, and stays free. The free plugin has no locked features, never expires, and is not a trial.

Gather Grove Booking Professional is a separate plugin, available from gathergrove.io, for studios that sell more than drop-ins. It adds:

  • Memberships and class packs
  • Gift cards
  • Family and household accounts
  • Multi-instructor scheduling
  • Enrollment-style courses
  • Custom email branding
  • Advanced reporting drill-downs

Compare every feature, line by line, at gathergrove.io/docs/pricing.

External services

This plugin connects to the following third-party services.

Stripe — used to process card payments after you connect a Stripe account and a client pays for a booking or appointment. The booking and payment details required to create the charge (amount, currency, and related metadata) are sent to Stripe at payment time. Stripe.js is loaded from Stripe’s servers on pages that display a payment form, as required for PCI compliance.
Terms of service: https://stripe.com/legal — Privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Google Maps — used by the optional Location “Map Embed” and “Directions Link” Elementor dynamic tags. If you place the Map Embed tag on a page, the visitor’s browser loads an embedded map from google.com for the location’s address (Google receives the visitor’s IP address and the studio address, as with any embedded map). The Directions Link tag only builds a link to google.com/maps containing the studio address; nothing is sent unless the visitor clicks it. No data is sent from your server, and neither tag is active unless you add it to a page.
Terms of service: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Zoom — used to automatically create, update, and delete Zoom meetings for virtual class and appointment sessions, only after you connect your own Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app under Settings → Integrations. When a virtual booking is confirmed (and on reschedule or cancellation), your server sends the session’s topic, start time, duration, timezone, and the host’s email address to api.zoom.us / zoom.us using your own credentials. Nothing is sent unless you enable the integration, and visitors’ browsers never contact Zoom through this plugin.
Terms of service: https://explore.zoom.us/en/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://explore.zoom.us/en/privacy/

Postmark — used to send your site’s email through your own Postmark account, only after you connect one under Gather Grove → Settings → Email delivery. When connected, your server sends Postmark your key, your sending domain (to register it and check its DNS records), and each email it is asked to send: sender, recipients, subject, body and any attachments. If you also switch on “Send all your site’s email through Postmark”, every email your site sends goes this way. Postmark then posts delivery, bounce, open, click, spam-complaint and unsubscribe reports back to a secret address on your site. Nothing is sent unless you connect an account.
Terms of service: https://postmarkapp.com/terms-of-service — Privacy policy: https://postmarkapp.com/privacy-policy

Web push services (Google, Mozilla, Apple, Microsoft) — when a member turns on phone notifications, their browser registers with its own push service, and your site sends each notification to that service for delivery. The notification carries a short title and a link. The push service receives it with the member’s browser subscription address, and with your site’s admin email address, which the web push standard requires as a contact for the sending site. Nothing is sent unless a member turns notifications on.
Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy — Mozilla privacy policy: https://www.mozilla.org/privacy/ — Apple privacy policy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/ — Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the free Elementor plugin (Plugins → Add New → search “Elementor”).
  2. Upload the gather-grove-booking folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  3. Activate Gather Grove Booking through the Plugins screen.
  4. Go to Gather Grove → Settings to configure your studio, then connect Stripe under the Payments tab.
  5. Use Gather Grove → Getting Started to create your booking and schedule pages.
sections.faq:
Do I need Elementor?

Yes — the free Elementor plugin (version 3.5 or newer) is required to display the booking form, schedule, and other client-facing pages. The admin and booking engine run without it, but your visitors need the Elementor widgets to book. If Elementor is older than 3.5 the widgets stay switched off and a notice asks you to update.

Do I need the other Gather Grove plugins?

No. Booking is complete on its own. The other Gather Grove plugins are optional and add email, communities, courses, forms and more when you want them.

Do I need Elementor Pro?

No. Elementor Pro is optional. It adds dynamic tags and automatic Theme Builder starter pages, but every booking feature works with the free Elementor plugin.

How are payments processed?

Card payments are processed by Stripe. You connect your own Stripe account; Gather Grove never stores card numbers on your site.

Does it work without a payment gateway?

Yes. You can run free classes, complimentary (comp) bookings, and offline/invoice payments without connecting Stripe.

Will my data be deleted if I uninstall?

No. Uninstalling leaves your studio data intact by default so you can reinstall safely. You can opt in to full data deletion under Settings → General → Danger Zone.

Does it change anything about my site’s login or security?

Two small protections are on by default, shared by every Gather Grove plugin. Visitors who are not logged in can no longer read your site’s list of account names (WordPress normally publishes it at /wp-json/wp/v2/users and through ?author= links). And after 10 failed logins from one address in 15 minutes, that address has to wait before trying again, on the WordPress login page and on Gather Grove’s own sign-in form. Logged-in editors are not affected, and sites behind Cloudflare are recognised automatically. If you already use a security plugin, or need the public account list, return false from the gather_grove/security/throttle_logins or gather_grove/security/hide_user_list filter to turn either off.

Can I style the widgets using my real classes in the Elementor editor?

Yes. Gather Grove widgets show a styleable sample by default in the Elementor editor. To style against your actual content, open the widget’s Content tab, find the “Editor Preview” section, and set “Preview in editor” to “Real data” (for the Class Card widget, also pick a specific class). The editor canvas then renders your real class so you can style it without switching to the live page. This is rolling out across the widgets — the Class Card and Sessions List widgets have it today, with more on the way. It only affects the editor; your published page always shows live data.

1.215.0

  • New: late fees for overdue memberships — set the fee, when it starts and how often it repeats; added to the member’s next invoice, stopped as soon as they pay, with waive and pause for staff. Off by default.
  • New: members can pay ahead with their saved card in one tap.
  • New: a month paid ahead is refunded automatically if the membership ends before it is invoiced.

1.214.1

  • Fix: changing your email delivery key for the same Postmark server no longer switches your site’s email off. Your Postmark Account token is no longer kept once your domain is verified, and a “Replace key” option replaces disconnecting.

1.214.0

  • New: a “payment due soon” email for memberships paid by invoice on a set day — a week before each due date, with what’s owed and a button to pay now. Not sent if the family has already paid. Replaces the renewal reminder for those memberships.

1.213.0

  • New: members who pay by invoice can pay from their account page — “Pay now” on an open invoice, or pay next month ahead of time. Paying ahead is held as credit and pays the invoice automatically on the due day.
  • Fix: a complimentary membership no longer says it is paid from a card; autopay no longer assumes a card.

1.212.1

  • Fix: on the account page, a membership’s payment line and its due day no longer run together.

1.212.0

  • New: “Due on day” for memberships. Bill every member on the same day of the month, such as tuition due on the 1st, whenever they joined. Invoices are sent on that day and due the same day; autopay is charged on it. Members see the day at checkout and on their account page. Off by default.

1.211.2

  • Maintenance: passes WordPress.org’s Plugin Check with no errors again. Nothing changes in how the plugin works.

1.211.1

  • Fixed: cancelling a booking could fail when the class already showed no seats taken. The seat is now returned safely and the count never goes below zero. The same fix covers approvals, waitlist releases and enrollment approvals.

1.211.0

  • New: got a closure’s dates wrong? Open it and press “Change dates”. Classes that fall outside the new dates go back on the schedule, and everyone who was booked gets one email saying the class is back on, with a link to book again. Classes inside the new dates are cancelled the usual way. You see exactly what changes before anything happens. Refunds are never taken back, and course dates are restored automatically.
  • New: ending a closure can now bring its classes back too. Tick “Also bring back its cancelled sessions” and they return to the schedule with open spots, with the same “back on” email.
  • Changed: Sessions → Closures is now “Closures & Bulk Cancels”, and its button is “Bulk cancel classes”, because it cancels some rooms, classes or instructors as often as the whole studio. The snow-day shortcuts are unchanged.
  • Changed: a closure that doesn’t cover the whole studio no longer tells clients the studio is closed. Its emails, reminders, account-page banner and notifications say the class is cancelled instead.
  • Changed: the closure preview shows the dates with the year and how far away they are (“starts in 11 days”), with a warning when they look unusual, and the confirm box repeats the dates.

1.210.0

  • New: with Gather Grove Pulse, every Booking email can be managed from Pulse → Messages — switch automations on and off, edit and reset the wording, preview it and send yourself a test. Edits are saved in Booking, so they stay if Pulse is switched off, and each email keeps a short edit history. While Pulse manages an email, Booking’s Email settings show it read-only with an “Edit in Pulse” link.
  • New: Booking’s marketing emails (birthday greeting, first-class follow-up, win-back and the rest) are now sent as marketing: they carry an Unsubscribe link and the one-click unsubscribe header mail providers expect. Someone who unsubscribes — here or from a Pulse email — stops getting marketing from both, but still gets confirmations, reminders and receipts.
  • Changed: emails to instructors and staff now end with “This is a staff notice from” your studio, instead of the member wording.
  • Fixed: saving the Email or Automated settings can no longer wipe wording or switches the form did not send.

1.209.0

  • Changed: the low sign-ups alert now goes to the class’s instructor and the studio admin, a week before the class by default (you can choose how many days). It watches each class’s own Minimum Enrollment and counts people, guests included. The email says plainly how many have signed up against the minimum, links to the class, and — if Gather Grove Pulse is promoting the class — to the promotion. Each class date gets at most one alert, and none if the date is cancelled or fills up first. It stays off until you switch it on under Settings → Email → Automated, where you can also turn off the instructor copy or watch classes without a minimum.

1.208.0

  • New: Gather Grove Pulse can now show what a class promotion achieved. Booking tells Pulse who signed up since the promotion started — including dependents and guest seats, cancellations and moves — and how much they paid after refunds, so Pulse can count sign-ups and revenue from its emails and early-bird code. The class editor’s Promote box and the Classes list show the results.
  • New: when you pause marketing email in Pulse, Booking’s own marketing automations (win-backs, follow-ups and so on) wait too — up to 7 days, then they are skipped. Class reminders, receipts and other operational email are never held.
  • New: Pulse can move a promotion’s early-bird code expiry when the class dates move.

1.207.0

  • New: works with Gather Grove Pulse’s “Promote this”. The class editor has a Promote box and the Classes list a Promote link: Pulse can send a short, well-timed series of emails about one class (or one date of a drop-in class) to people who already know you — past students, last time’s group, this category’s regulars — with an optional early-bird code that only works for that class. Without Pulse, administrators see a one-line note instead.
  • Fixed: a relative registration close on a course-style class (for example “closes 1 day before”) was measured from midnight UTC instead of midnight at the studio, so enrollment closed 4–5 hours early in North American time zones. It now closes at the right local time, including across daylight-saving changes.

1.206.2

  • Fixed: when a membership belongs to a child with no email of their own, renewal reminders, payment warnings and package emails now go to the parent who pays, and say which child they’re about. Before, they were skipped without anyone knowing.
  • Fixed: the “membership renews soon” reminder now goes out before every renewal, not only the first one.

1.206.1

  • Fixed: on sites with smooth scrolling and a sticky header (common with Elementor themes), the calendar’s class details popup could end up over the header with its title cut off. It now appears once the page has stopped scrolling, stays clear of the header, fits a long popup by scrolling inside it, and closes when its class scrolls out of view.

1.206.0

  • New: works with Gather Grove Pulse’s automations. When you switch on a Pulse version of a Booking email (such as the no-show follow-up), Booking steps aside so nobody gets two copies, and takes over again by itself if Pulse’s version is paused. Settings → Email → Automated shows which plugin sends each email, with “Send from Booking instead” and “Let Pulse send it” buttons.
  • New: with Pulse active, Booking’s marketing emails respect Pulse’s weekly limit on marketing email per person. A held-back email waits a day and tries again, and is skipped if it can’t go out within two days of when it was due. Operational emails are never held back.

1.205.0

  • New: checkout now asks for the waiver BEFORE payment — your details, then the waiver (only if one is owed), then payment, then confirm — on class bookings, appointments, bundles, class packs, memberships and courses. People read and sign the terms before they type a card number. Returning clients who have already signed see no extra step.
  • Fixed: on a dark site the booking page card showed as a grey panel, and anything shown directly on it (the waiver form, notices, the confirmation) was hard to read. The card now uses your studio’s own colours.
  • Fixed: the first click on “Confirm Booking” after typing in the form sometimes did nothing, and a class pack you had picked could switch back to the drop-in option. One click now books, and your choice stays.
  • Fixed: a guest enrolling in a course, buying a class pack with a booking, or buying an appointment bundle no longer gets an account (and a welcome email) when the checkout is refused for a reason like “no upcoming sessions” or an unavailable time.

1.204.0

  • Fixed: a guest buying a class pack with a booking, enrolling in a course, or buying an appointment bundle, who had to sign a waiver first, was told “An account already exists for that email address. Please log in” when the booking carried on after signing. The checkout now recognises the account it created a moment earlier and finishes. An account that already existed, or whose owner has since signed in, is still asked to log in.

1.203.0

  • New: a waiver built in Gather Grove Forms is now filled in right inside checkout, like any other waiver. The form appears in the booking, and the booking carries on as soon as it is submitted — for members, parents booking for their children, and guests. The “Form page” setting is now optional and only used for emailed and portal links. Needs Gather Grove Forms 1.33.0 or newer.
  • New: guests who fill in a waiver form do not have to fill it in again for 24 hours on the same browser, as long as they book with the same email.
  • New: if a waiver’s form cannot be shown (Forms switched off or too old, the form archived, or the form takes a payment), bookings that need it are refused with a clear message, and a notice in your dashboard names the waiver and the form. The waiver’s settings warn about forms that take a payment or redirect.
  • Security: a guest checkout is no longer given a permanent signing link for the account behind the email they typed.
  • Security: a waiver that uses a form can only be signed by completing that form — never by an “I agree” tick, including on appointments, the sign-ahead page and emailed signing pages.

1.202.0

  • New: close the studio from Sessions → Closures. Pick the day (or the hours), whether it is the whole studio or only some locations, rooms, classes or instructors, and see every class it would cancel — with the bookings, people and money involved — before anything happens. Untick anything that should still run.
  • New: “Snow day: close today” and “Close tomorrow” buttons on the Sessions screen set up an all-day closure for the whole studio and take you straight to that preview.
  • New: when you confirm, every class in the closure is cancelled and everyone gets their money back the way they paid: cards are refunded (or, if you choose, turned into studio credit), class-pack sessions, session credits and studio credit come back, and unpaid invoices are cancelled. Course dates are simply dropped; the course carries on. Memberships are not changed.
  • New: each client gets one email listing every booking the closure cancelled and what happened to it. A parent who booked for their children gets one email listing each child’s seat. Waitlisted clients and instructors get their own single email, and managers get a summary. Clients and instructors are reminded the day before, unless the closure was announced at short notice.
  • New: a “Studio closed” notice on the client account page and the instructor dashboard during the week before and during a closure.
  • New: only Studio Directors, Gather Grove Admins and site administrators can close the studio. Managers can see the list of closures.

Older releases are listed in changelog.txt, included with the plugin and viewable at https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/gather-grove-booking/trunk/changelog.txt

short_description: For yoga studios, teachers, and community programs — class booking, waivers, appointments, waitlists, and Stripe payments. Built for Elementor.
description:
Gather Grove Booking runs the schedule for people who teach — yoga and fitness studios, dance and martial arts schools, music teachers, pottery and craft studios, wellness practitioners, and community programs. Design your booking pages visually with Elementor, take drop-in and appointment bookings, and accept card payments with Stripe.

The free version is fully functional for running a real studio:

  • Classes & sessions — recurring schedules, capacity limits, multiple locations and rooms.
  • Online booking — Elementor booking-form and schedule widgets your clients use to reserve a spot.
  • Appointments — bookable service slots with availability windows and optional deposits.
  • Waivers & liability forms — collect a real signature as part of booking, then see your whole roster at a glance: who has signed the current version, who signed an older one, whose signature has expired, and who has never signed at all. Send reminders by hand, record a paper signature, or export the lot to CSV.
  • Passwordless sign-in — students can sign in with a link emailed to them instead of a password, so nobody is locked out of a booking by a password they never set. Optional, and you choose whether your site offers passwords, magic links, or both.
  • Waitlists — clients can join a waitlist when a class is full, and open spots are automatically offered to the next person in line.
  • Flexible schedules — a class can meet on multiple recurring schedule blocks (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri at different times).
  • Bulk attendance marking — mark a whole roster present in one action.
  • Payments — accept cards through Stripe for drop-in bookings.
  • Client accounts — a self-service dashboard for bookings and profile.
  • Attendance — front-desk and instructor check-in.
  • Instructors & locations — profiles, assignments, and per-location schedules.

Who it’s for

  • Yoga, pilates and fitness studios — recurring drop-in classes, capacity limits, waitlists, and a signed waiver on file before anyone steps on a mat.
  • Dance and martial arts schools — several weekly schedule blocks on one class, per-location rooms, and front-desk check-in.
  • Music teachers and schools — appointment-style lessons with availability windows and optional deposits, alongside recurring group classes.
  • Pottery, craft and maker studios — small capacities, multiple rooms, and a roster you can mark present in one action.
  • Wellness practitioners — one-to-one appointments shown in the visitor’s own timezone, with a self-service client dashboard.
  • Breathwork, meditation and sound-healing facilitators — circles, workshops and sound baths with capacity limits, a waitlist when they fill, and a waiver signed before anyone arrives.
  • Coaches, mentors and private sessions — bookable one-to-one slots with availability windows and optional deposits, so clients pick a time without the back-and-forth.
  • Online facilitators — virtual classes and appointments, with the Zoom meeting created for you and the join link in every confirmation and reminder.
  • Community programs and co-ops — free and comp bookings with no payment gateway required, and waiver compliance across a whole roster.

Built for Elementor

The client-facing pages (booking form, class schedule, appointment booking, client dashboard) are Elementor widgets, so you design them visually alongside the rest of your site. The free Elementor plugin (3.5 or newer) is required to display these on your site. Elementor Pro is optional — it adds dynamic tags and one-click Theme Builder starter pages, but is not required for booking to work.

Part of the Gather Grove suite

Gather Grove Booking works entirely on its own. It is also one part of Gather Grove, a family of plugins for running and growing a creative business on your own WordPress site. The plugins share one admin, one list of people, and one look, so a studio can add what it needs as it grows:

  • Gather Grove Pulse — email broadcasts, automated sequences and a contact list that knows who booked, joined or enrolled.
  • Gather Grove Communities — private member spaces with rooms, an activity feed and direct messages.
  • Gather Grove Courses — self-paced and cohort-based online courses.
  • Gather Grove Forms — applications, intake forms and RSVPs that feed the rest of the suite.
  • Gather Grove Companion — an AI assistant for your admin, and a chat helper for your visitors.
  • Gather Grove Notion Sync — free; sends bookings and form entries to your Notion workspace.

Together they serve creators, mentors, facilitators and anyone running a private community or an online program, as well as studios. Learn more at gathergrove.io.

External services

This plugin connects to the following third-party services.

Stripe — used to process card payments after you connect a Stripe account and a client pays for a booking or appointment. The booking and payment details required to create the charge (amount, currency, and related metadata) are sent to Stripe at payment time. Stripe.js is loaded from Stripe’s servers on pages that display a payment form, as required for PCI compliance.
Terms of service: https://stripe.com/legal — Privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Google Maps — used by the optional Location “Map Embed” and “Directions Link” Elementor dynamic tags. If you place the Map Embed tag on a page, the visitor’s browser loads an embedded map from google.com for the location’s address (Google receives the visitor’s IP address and the studio address, as with any embedded map). The Directions Link tag only builds a link to google.com/maps containing the studio address; nothing is sent unless the visitor clicks it. No data is sent from your server, and neither tag is active unless you add it to a page.
Terms of service: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Zoom — used to automatically create, update, and delete Zoom meetings for virtual class and appointment sessions, only after you connect your own Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app under Settings → Integrations. When a virtual booking is confirmed (and on reschedule or cancellation), your server sends the session’s topic, start time, duration, timezone, and the host’s email address to api.zoom.us / zoom.us using your own credentials. Nothing is sent unless you enable the integration, and visitors’ browsers never contact Zoom through this plugin.
Terms of service: https://explore.zoom.us/en/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://explore.zoom.us/en/privacy/

Postmark — used to send your site’s email through your own Postmark account, only after you connect one under Gather Grove → Settings → Email delivery. When connected, your server sends Postmark your key, your sending domain (to register it and check its DNS records), and each email it is asked to send: sender, recipients, subject, body and any attachments. If you also switch on “Send all your site’s email through Postmark”, every email your site sends goes this way. Postmark then posts delivery, bounce, open, click, spam-complaint and unsubscribe reports back to a secret address on your site. Nothing is sent unless you connect an account.
Terms of service: https://postmarkapp.com/terms-of-service — Privacy policy: https://postmarkapp.com/privacy-policy

Web push services (Google, Mozilla, Apple, Microsoft) — when a member turns on phone notifications, their browser registers with its own push service, and your site sends each notification to that service for delivery. The notification carries a short title and a link. The push service receives it with the member’s browser subscription address, and with your site’s admin email address, which the web push standard requires as a contact for the sending site. Nothing is sent unless a member turns notifications on.
Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy — Mozilla privacy policy: https://www.mozilla.org/privacy/ — Apple privacy policy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/ — Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
